messages:
Alex G: Heads up — ap-south edge proxy started throwing TLS verify errors and dropping connections around 14:02 UTC after cert-rotator canary hit 3/3.
Maria P: logs? can you paste error lines?
Alex G: proxy stderr snippet:
```
2026-03-21T14:02:18Z proxy[edge-1]: TLS verify error: x509:certificate signed by unknown authority (certificate verification loop detected)
2026-03-21T14:02:19Z proxy[edge-2]: TLS handshake failed: chain validation resulted in a cycle
```
Cheng L: "certificate verification loop" typically means a duplicate intermediate or root appended to the chain. dump the secret the rotator wrote.
Alex G: `kubectl -n certs get secret edge-cert -o yaml` shows tls.crt chain decodes to: leaf -> intermediate A -> intermediate A -> root CA (duplicate intermediate).
Jonah S: rotator logs show it concatenated intermediate.pem twice for ap-south during canary. KMS unwraps look normal; the bug is chain assembly.
rotator-bot: canary rollout completed for cert-rotator v2 (3 pods) — 14:01 UTC ✅
Maria P: any recent RBAC/SA changes that might redirect the rotator to fallback artifacts?
Alex G: cert-rotator service account had secretmanager.versions.access widened 48h ago (PR #872) — noted.
Cheng L: quick cross-region check: `gcloud secrets versions access --secret=cert-chain-ap-south --format=json` shows payload with duplicate intermediate only in ap-south; eu-west OK.
Jonah S: hypothesis: rotator fallback path appended fallback-intermediate when primary was briefly unavailable, both appended producing duplicate.
Maria P: scope/impact?
Alex G: affected: ap-south edge -> internal workers that strictly validate chains. ~3% errors observed; spike 13:59–14:10.
Cheng L: mitigation options — rollback canary, hotfix assembly to dedupe, restart proxies after secret fix.
Jonah S: quick remediation script to normalize chain and reload secret (tested in staging):
```
# strip duplicate cert blocks
awk 'BEGIN{RS="-----END CERTIFICATE-----";ORS=""} {if(!seen[$0]++){print $0 "-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"}}' chain.pem > normalized.pem
kubectl -n certs create secret tls edge-cert --cert=normalized.pem --key=... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n proxy rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy
```
Alex G: pull KMS audit for unwraps 13:58–14:05 to confirm no tamper.
Maria P: grabbing Cloud KMS audit and Secret Manager access logs now. Also checking rotator uses correct secret name.
rotator-bot: detected config drift: rotator-template v2 references intermediate.pem and intermediate-fallback.pem from same bucket; no write perms changed.
Jonah S: opened PR #891 with dedupe algorithm + verification gate to reject assembled chains with repeated fingerprints and unit tests.
Cheng L: agree rollback first to restore traffic. record incident root cause "chain assembly appended duplicate intermediate". then patch + canary.
Alex G: rolling back: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deployment/cert-rotator --to-revision=18`
deploy-bot: rollback started for cert-rotator to revision 18 — triggered by @Alex G at 14:12 UTC
Maria P: KMS audit shows unwrap events normal, no denies. Secret Manager shows writes at 14:01 and 14:03 by rotator-sa.
Jonah S: after rollback I applied the normalized chain to one edge pod; errors dropped to ~0.8% within 5m.
Cheng L: follow-ups: add chain-normalization in rotator assembly; add unit/e2e tests for duplicate intermediates; add gating check `openssl verify -CAfile <root> <assembled_chain>` and fail assembly if cycles detected; add Secret Manager write alert if chain length delta > threshold.
Maria P: update RBAC playbook: enumerate who can push certs, require approval hook for canary >1 region.
Alex G: creating incident postmortem stub, tagging security and SRE; will include timeline, audit snippets, PR link.
Jonah S: postmortem notes: impacted service internal ingestion -> ap-south; duration ~14:02–14:15; root cause: rotator concatenation fallback bug.
rotator-bot: canary rollback completed — 14:14 UTC ✅
Alex G: owners: Jonah -> hotfix & tests; Maria -> audit & RBAC update; Cheng -> rollout gating verification; I'll author the PM/incident doc.
Maria P: filing follow-ups in triage board and assigning priorities.
Jonah S: adding unit tests against malformed chains to ensure detection of verification loops.
Alex G: closing thread once postmortem link posted. :thumbsup:
